# Key numbers (generated by scripts/make_readme_charts.py)

## Headline

Cheapest setting that meets 95%: **Optimiser, freelancers only, P90, pre-screen on**, 95.9% on time, 2,678k a year.

Cheapest without the pre-screen: **EDF + due-date check, planned mix, P80, pre-screen off**, 96.1%, 3,232k.

33 of 72 settings meet the target.

## Chart takeaways (the computed titles)

- `headline.png`: Cheapest way to stay on time at 4x: Optimiser, freelancers only, P90, pre-screen on, 2,678k a year
- `mix.png`: Freelancers only is the cheapest way to meet 95% (2,678k); full-timers only costs 236k more
- `policies.png`: At the default plan, Optimiser with the pre-screen is the cheapest way to meet 95% (2,735k); without it, EDF + due-date check (3,232k)
- `growth.png`: Earliest deadline first narrowly misses 95% at 1x and 2x; EDF + due-date check meets 95% at every growth level; Optimiser meets 95% at every growth level; cost rises 2.0x from 1x to 4x
- `forecast_error.png`: Hiring for 2x when 4x arrives loses 36.5 pts of on-time and adds 1,882k; hiring for 6x gains 1.2 pts of on-time and adds 661k
- `baseline.png`: Without hiring, 4x growth overwhelms the team: the best setting (Optimiser, pre-screen on) delivers only 37% on time
- `cadence.png`: Assigning work daily instead of weekly adds 28.3 pts on time on average (27.3–29.0 pts across rules)
- `policy_gain.png`: The optimiser's gain over first come, first served grows as capacity tightens: up to +20.7 pts on time and -28.9% cost
- `paired.png`: Optimiser beats first come, first served on both on-time and cost in 12 of 18 staffing settings
- `late_penalty.png`: Optimiser is the cheapest rule that meets 95% at every late penalty (250–4,000); among those, EDF + due-date check spends least excluding penalties; Earliest deadline first never reaches 95%
